title: TypeScript Quiz
description: Fourteen questions covering the whole TypeScript tutorial: the compiler, basic types, functions, interfaces, modules, tuples, enums, classes, generics, narrowing, utility types, async code, strict mode and declaration files.

questions.question: What happens to interfaces and type annotations when `tsc` compiles a file?
questions.explanation: Types exist only at compile time. The emitted JavaScript contains no annotations, interfaces or type aliases and performs no type checks.
options: They are converted into runtime checks that throw on wrong types
They are removed; the JavaScript output contains no types
They are kept as comments so the browser can read them
They are moved into a separate JavaScript file

questions.question: Setting `"strict": true` in tsconfig.json enables `noImplicitAny` and `strictNullChecks` at the same time.
questions.explanation: strict is a shortcut for a family of flags that includes noImplicitAny, strictNullChecks, strictPropertyInitialization, useUnknownInCatchVariables and more.

questions.question: The type that accepts any value but must be narrowed before you can call methods on it is `___`.
questions.explanation: unknown is the type-safe counterpart of any: everything is assignable to it, but it cannot be used until a check such as typeof proves what it holds.

questions.question: `function add(a: number, b: number): number` is called as `add(1)`. What does the compiler report?
questions.explanation: Argument counts are checked. Calling with one argument produces TS2554: Expected 2 arguments, but got 1, together with a note pointing at the parameter that was not provided.
options: TS2322: Type 'undefined' is not assignable to type 'number'
A runtime error when the function executes

questions.question: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: task is a variable, not a fresh object literal, so the excess property check does not apply. It has an id of type number, which is all HasId requires, so the call compiles and prints #3.
options: A compiler error, because `title` is not in `HasId`

questions.question: In a project with `"module": "nodenext"` and `"type": "module"`, which import of the local file `src/dates.ts` compiles?
questions.explanation: The compiler never rewrites import paths, so you write the path that exists after compilation. ./dates.js resolves to dates.ts while checking and to dist/dates.js at runtime.

questions.question: Why does this line fail to compile?
questions.explanation: A tuple type fixes the type of each position. The first element must be a string and the second a number; the literal has them swapped, so tsc reports two TS2322 errors.
options: Tuples cannot mix strings and numbers
The elements are in the wrong order for the tuple type
The tuple needs a third element

questions.question: Given `enum LogLevel { Info = "info" }` and `function log(level: LogLevel)`, the call `log("info")` is accepted.
questions.explanation: String enums are nominal: only the enum member LogLevel.Info is accepted, even though its value is the same string. A literal union would accept the plain string.

questions.question: Where may a `readonly` class property be assigned?
questions.explanation: readonly allows assignment in the property declaration and inside the constructor only. Any later assignment, including from methods of the same class, is a TS2540 error.
options: From any method of the class, but not from outside
Only in the declaration or in the constructor
Never; a readonly property has no value

questions.question: In `function first<T>(items: T[]): T | undefined`, the `T` declared in angle brackets is called a type ___.
questions.explanation: T is a type parameter (also called a type variable): a placeholder that the compiler replaces with a concrete type at each call, either by inference or from an explicit type argument.

questions.question: What does this program print?
questions.explanation: ok is the discriminant. When it is true the compiler narrows result to the member with value; when it is false, to the member with error. The first call prints error nope and the second value 7.
options: A compiler error: `value` does not exist on type `Result`

questions.question: What does `Partial<User>` produce?
questions.explanation: Partial is a mapped type that adds ? to every property. It is typically used for update payloads where any subset of fields may be supplied.
options: A type where every property of `User` is read-only
A type with all of `User`'s properties made optional
A type with only the first property of `User`

questions.question: What is the return type of `async function load() { return "ready"; }`?
questions.explanation: An async function always returns a promise. The returned string becomes the resolved value, so the type is Promise<string>; await load() gives a string.

questions.question: A `.d.ts` file contains only type declarations and produces no JavaScript when compiled.
questions.explanation: Declaration files describe the types of code that lives elsewhere, such as a JavaScript package or your own compiled library. They are never emitted as JavaScript.
